classification.difficultyReason: Identify the high outlier on the right and infer that removing its upward pull makes the negative fitted gradient more negative and the line steeper.

content.prompt:
A survey collected data on cars with a 50 L petrol tank.
It compared distance driven and litres of petrol remaining in the tank.

spec.description: Unit grid with numbered ticks 1–10, arrowed axes, axis titles, thirteen points and a supplied descending fitted line. Non-outlier point positions and fitted-line endpoints are approximate visual reconstructions, not exact numerical givens.
spec.mathematics: The supplied outlier is (6.9,9.8). The other twelve observations follow a negative association. Removing the high outlier makes the fitted gradient more negative.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied fitted line is permanent question content. The outlier circle appears only in the solution.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Identify the outlier. Circle the data point.

answer.worked: Circle $(6.9,9.8)$, which lies well above the negative trend of the other points.

spec.description: Solution-only circle around the supplied outlier, using the base graph's exact coordinate units, origin and bounding box.

children.label: b
children.prompt: If the outlier were removed, what would happen to the gradient of the line of best fit? Would it be steeper or less steep?

answer.worked: The high outlier pulls the right-hand end of the fitted line upwards. Removing it makes the line slope downwards more steeply, so its gradient becomes more negative.
